issues.legal_issue: Procedural defects in imposing a municipal tax do not invalidate the levy when the defects are not fundamental and cause no substantial prejudice, and an official notification of imposition is conclusive proof that the statutory steps were taken.
material_facts: The Board had authority to impose the water tax and passed the special resolution directing its imposition.
The prescribed authority notified the imposition of the tax in the official gazette.
There were procedural defects in publishing the preliminary proposal, the modified proposal, and the special resolution.
The inhabitants had notice of the proposal and the imposition, and the defects did not cause substantial prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The procedural defects did not invalidate the tax levy; the notification of imposition was conclusive proof that the necessary steps had been taken.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 135(3) of the U.P. Municipalities Act, 1916, notification under section 135(2) is conclusive proof that the tax was imposed in accordance with the Act. Procedural defects that are not fundamental and cause no substantial prejudice to inhabitants are cured and do not invalidate the levy. The Court applied Municipal Board v. Raghuvendra, [1966] 1 S.C.R. 950; Buland Sugar v. Municipal Board, [1965] 1 S.C.R. 970; and Berar Swadeshi Vanaspathi v. Municipal Committee, Shegaon, [1962] 1 S.C.R. 596.

rule.if: municipal_tax_levy_challenge and board_authorized_to_levy_tax and imposition_resolution_passed and official_imposition_notification_issued and not fundamental_procedural_defect and not substantial_prejudice

predicates.municipal_tax_levy_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a municipal tax levy.
predicates.board_authorized_to_levy_tax: The municipal body had authority to impose the tax.
predicates.imposition_resolution_passed: The municipal body passed a resolution directing imposition of the tax.
predicates.official_imposition_notification_issued: The prescribed authority issued an official notification imposing the tax.
predicates.fundamental_procedural_defect: A defect in the procedure for imposing the tax was fundamental.
predicates.substantial_prejudice: The procedural defect caused substantial prejudice to the municipality’s inhabitants.
predicates.procedural_defects_do_not_invalidate_tax: The procedural defects do not invalidate the tax levy.

issues.definition: When a municipal tax levy is challenged, the body had authority and passed an imposition resolution, an official notification was issued, and the procedural defects were neither fundamental nor substantially prejudicial, the defects do not invalidate the levy.

issues.legal_issue: A preliminary tax proposal is sufficiently published when its substance is included in published draft rules and the publication informs inhabitants of the proposal so they can object.
material_facts: The draft rules and notice were published in a local newspaper.
The published draft rules included the preliminary proposal and identified the resolution framing it.
The proposal was not separately published in the prescribed form.
Inhabitants filed objections, and the Board considered them.
issues.conclusion: The publication substantially complied with the publication requirement; the failure to publish the proposal separately was a mere irregularity and did not invalidate the levy.
issues.legal_principle: Section 131(3), read with section 94 of the U.P. Municipalities Act, 1916, requires publication of the proposal and draft rules to inform inhabitants and enable objections. Where publication of the draft rules incorporates the proposal and achieves that purpose, omission of separate publication is an irregularity. The Court applied Buland Sugar v. Municipal Board, [1965] 1 S.C.R. 970, and the principle in Municipal Board v. Raghuvendra, [1966] 1 S.C.R. 950, concerning the curative effect of section 135(3).

rule.if: municipal_tax_levy_challenge and proposal_included_in_published_draft_rules and inhabitants_informed_of_proposal and inhabitants_able_to_object

predicates.municipal_tax_levy_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a municipal tax levy.
predicates.proposal_included_in_published_draft_rul: The published draft rules contained the substance of the preliminary tax proposal.
predicates.inhabitants_informed_of_proposal: The publication gave inhabitants notice of the proposed tax.
predicates.inhabitants_able_to_object: Inhabitants had an opportunity to submit objections to the proposal.
predicates.preliminary_publication_defect_is_irregu: The failure to publish the preliminary proposal separately is a mere irregularity.

issues.definition: In a challenge to a municipal tax levy, if the published draft rules contain the proposal and inform inhabitants so they can object, failure to publish the proposal separately is a mere irregularity.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to publish a modified tax proposal does not invalidate the levy when inhabitants had an opportunity to object to the original rate and exemption limit and the modification caused no prejudice.
material_facts: The original proposal set a higher tax rate and a lower exemption limit than the modified proposal.
The Board considered inhabitants’ objections and reduced the proposed rate and raised the exemption limit.
The modified proposal was not separately published, so inhabitants were not invited to file fresh objections.
Inhabitants had previously been able to object to the proposed rate and exemption limit, and no prejudice resulted from the omission.
issues.conclusion: Non-publication of the modified proposal was a mere irregularity, and the defect was cured.
issues.legal_principle: Section 132(2) of the U.P. Municipalities Act, 1916, required publication of a modified proposal. However, where inhabitants had an opportunity to object to the original rate and exemption limit, and the modification reduced the rate or raised the exemption limit without causing prejudice, non-publication is an irregularity cured by section 135(3). The Court also noted that a later amendment to section 132(2) exempted publication where a modification reduced the tax, although that amendment was not in force at the relevant time.

rule.if: municipal_tax_levy_challenge and original_rate_and_exemption_open_to_objection and modification_reduced_rate_or_raised_exemption and no_fresh_objections_invited and no_prejudice_from_nonpublication

predicates.municipal_tax_levy_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a municipal tax levy.
predicates.original_rate_and_exemption_open_to_obje: Inhabitants had an opportunity to object to the originally proposed tax rate and exemption limit.
predicates.modification_reduced_rate_or_raised_exem: The modification reduced the proposed tax rate or raised the exemption limit.
predicates.no_fresh_objections_invited: Inhabitants were not invited to submit fresh objections to the modified proposal.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_nonpublication: The failure to publish the modified proposal caused no prejudice to inhabitants.
predicates.modified_proposal_nonpublication_is_irre: Failure to publish the modified proposal is a mere irregularity.

issues.definition: In a challenge to a municipal tax levy, where inhabitants could object to the original rate and exemption limit, the modification reduced the rate or raised the exemption, and non-publication caused no prejudice, omission of a fresh invitation to object is a mere irregularity.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to publish the resolution directing imposition of a tax does not invalidate the levy when the governing provision does not require publication and inhabitants receive official notice of the imposition.
material_facts: The provision authorizing the Board to direct imposition of the tax did not require publication of that resolution.
The resolution directing imposition was not published in the manner prescribed by the general publication provision.
The inhabitants had no right to file objections to that resolution.
The prescribed authority published an official notification of the imposition of the tax.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming publication of the resolution was required, its non-publication was a mere irregularity cured by section 135(3).
issues.legal_principle: Section 134(2) of the U.P. Municipalities Act, 1916, does not provide for publication of the resolution directing imposition of the tax. Even assuming section 94 required such publication, its omission is an irregularity cured by section 135(3), where inhabitants had no right to object to the resolution and had notice of the imposition through the official notification.

rule.if: municipal_tax_levy_challenge and imposition_resolution_not_published and inhabitants_had_no_right_to_object_to_resolution and official_imposition_notice_given

predicates.municipal_tax_levy_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a municipal tax levy.
predicates.imposition_resolution_not_published: The resolution directing imposition of the tax was not published.
predicates.inhabitants_had_no_right_to_object_to_re: Inhabitants had no right to submit objections to the resolution directing imposition.
predicates.official_imposition_notice_given: Inhabitants received notice of the tax imposition through an official notification.
predicates.resolution_nonpublication_does_not_inval: Failure to publish the imposition resolution does not invalidate the tax levy.

issues.definition: In a challenge to a municipal tax levy, when the imposition resolution was not published, inhabitants had no right to object to it, and they received official notice of the imposition, the non-publication does not invalidate the levy.
